result.title: Teacher-Guided Tool Learning for Small Language Models via Bidirectional KL Constraints
result.summary: External tools can extend the capabilities of small language models (SLMs), enabling their deployment in resource constrained environments. However, their limited capabilities make it difficult for SLMs to discover effective tool use behaviors through reinforcement learning alone, while direct teacher supervision suffers from teacher student behavioral distribution mismatch and may propagate erroneous preferences. To address these challenges, we propose Selective Teacher guided Policy Optimization (SeTPO), which coordinates student exploration with selective teacher guidance and persistent demonstration supervision. Specifically, SeTPO incorporates reverse KL derived token level teacher feedback into policy advantages on low reward trajectories, while auxiliary forward KL supervision preserves teacher demonstrated behaviors throughout training. Under an idealized bidirectional KL objective, we theoretically establish that the optimal policy achieves expected reward no lower than the teacher's while retaining a guaranteed fraction of the teacher's probability mass. Extensive experiments on BFCL v4 and API Bank demonstrate that SeTPO achieves superior overall performance over supervised fine tuning, reinforcement learning, and distillation baselines across all three student scales.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SeTPO：在低奖励轨迹上把反向 KL 得到的 token 级教师反馈并入策略优势，并用前向 KL 辅助监督维持教师示范行为，从而让小型语言模型学到工具调用能力，在 BFCL v4 与 API Bank 上对比 SFT、RL 与蒸馏基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及视觉或多模态 latent 状态，但其「按轨迹质量选择性地注入 token 级双向 KL 约束、并保证保留一定教师概率质量」的做法，可能为 latent 推理轨迹训练中的监督选择与信息坍缩问题提供可核查的方法线索。
